First if you have got blood , phone to Abbott, they should replace the sensor because values will stay erratic and false. Normally this replacement is free of charge. Do not take off the sensor since Abbott ask for.
For your question, the two low and high are dangerous but not on the same way:
The low is quickly dangerous: too low values can create a coma ( very dangerous) when we are at 3.6 it is a warning..and you right eating sugar.
The high is dangerous on a long term basis, sugar will have an effect on your some vessels (eyes), and extremities ( fingers, toes..)
So a strict attitude to stay between green values will be ok. Your spreadsheets are the good way to monitor your t2 diabetes.
